messages:
maria: heads up — bringing up northstar-11b (int4) on Dedicated tonight. seeing reproducible OOM spikes during warmup + a small rouge drop on summarization eval vs float baseline. posting quick notes. :wave:

jon: can you paste the runner config + a minimal repro?

maria: sure — config we used (simplified):

```
model: northstar-11b-int4
batch_size: 4
max_new_tokens: 128
kv_prefetch: true
slot_compact_threshold: 0.2
soft_reserve: 0.12
```

maria: repro pattern: cold start, run 10 concurrent short chats (~200 tokens) then send one long summarize prompt (~3k tokens). after the long one, host hits an OOM and later recovers after compaction. Logs show KV cache growing steadily during the long response.

tess: do you have the GPU malloc trace / slab stats? even a snippet helps.

maria: pasted relevant lines from node logs:

```
[2026-03-23T01:12:04Z] alloc 1.2GiB failed -> OOM
[2026-03-23T01:12:05Z] kv_cache_size: 3.8GiB
[2026-03-23T01:12:05Z] slot_free_fraction: 0.04
[2026-03-23T01:12:07Z] compactor: reclaimed 620MiB
```

kevin: hmm. two levers that worked for other int4 brings: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens for this model to 32 (long tails trigger kv growth), 2) enable aggressive kv-trim-for-long-resp (trim older prefixes when generation > 512 tokens).

alex-sre: also consider a microbatch pacing tweak — add a 40–60ms inter-batch sleep to avoid burst allocation spikes. we saw p95 latency impact ~+6% but it reduced OOMs for similar models.

jon: are we seeing quality regression only at long summaries or across prompts?

maria: the rouge drop is concentrated on long-form summarization suites (summaries > 800 tokens). for short summaries/generation quality matches float baseline within noise. hypothesis: quantization + our current KV packing leads to token truncation/precision loss when sequence gets long. need to run a targeted eval.

tess: propose canary plan: rollback-safe defaults + telemetry. steps:
- lower max_new_tokens default to 32 for northstar-11b-int4
- enable kv trim at 512 token boundary
- apply batch_pacing_ms = 50
- enable slot compactor to run more frequently (run_interval = 30s) on canary hosts
- run summarization eval harness (140 examples) + perf harness (p50/p95 tokens)

maria: sounds good. I'll open PR with the config change and a canary rollout (5% of dedicated pool). aiming for the canary to run 2k requests over the next 6 hours.

maria: minimal curl to hit canary (replace API_KEY):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://dedicated-canary.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Model: northstar-11b-int4" \
  -d '{"input":"<long summarize prompt>","max_new_tokens":32}'
```

kevin: evaluation targets: p95 token latency < 140ms, memory cushion >= 512MiB after warmup, rouge >= float_baseline - 0.8 absolute. if we hit rouge drop > 0.8 then cut quant rollout and run per-layer analysis.

alex-sre: I'll queue a kernel-sched/defrag patch to the canary hosts too (patch id: infra/defrag/2026-03-23-7). small chance it helps slab churn.

deploy-bot: :robot_face: canary policy updated — northstar-11b-int4 defaults -> 5% Dedicated canary. PR: #1423 created by maria.

jon: thanks — ping me when PR lands, i'll wire the eval harness and compare against baseline metrics.

maria: will do. updating thread with PR link and eval results soon. :mag:
